subject: sand dune desert
title: Some Sand Dunes Sing Louder Than a Motorcycle, for 15 Minutes

scenes.text: In a few deserts, the sand itself starts to sing.
The hum can reach 105 decibels, louder than a motorcycle, and carry six miles.
It can last fifteen minutes. Marco Polo blamed desert spirits.
Only about three dozen places on Earth do it. It needs hot, dry sand sliding down a steep face.
The grains slam together about a hundred times a second, all in step, and the dune works like a loudspeaker.
And smaller grains sing higher notes. Every dune has its own pitch.

description:
Booming dunes can reach about 105 decibels, be heard up to 10 km away and keep humming for up to 15 minutes. Marco Polo wrote of desert sands that sounded like drums and instruments.
Only about 35 sites are known. The sound comes from a thin, synchronised avalanche of dry grains on a steep slip face; finer grains give higher notes, from about 60 Hz in Nevada to 105 Hz in Morocco.
Would you camp next to a dune that sings?
first_comment: Marco Polo thought it was spirits. What do you think the first people to hear a singing dune believed?
